title.value: Predicting Tactical Solutions to Operational Planning Problems under Imperfect Information
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the paper.
title.quote: Predicting Tactical Solutions to Operational Planning Problems under Imperfect Information

extractions.description: This paper presents a methodology that integrates machine learning and operations research to predict Tactical Descriptions of Operational Solutions (TDOSs) quickly under imperfect information, specifically in two-stage stochastic programming contexts. The approach allows for faster decision-making in operational planning without the need for detailed second-stage scenario generation, with a focus on applications in rail transportation planning.

primary_category.justification: The paper is closely related to efficient transportation planning, which can significantly contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the transportation sector, a key area in Climate Change Mitigation.
primary_category.quote: Results on our motivating application on load planning for rail transportation show that deep learning models produce accurate predictions in very short computing time...

secondary_categories.justification: Efficient planning in transportation can also aid in adapting to the impacts of climate change by optimizing resource use and improving resilience in infrastructure operations.
secondary_categories.quote: The problem we address occurs in the context of two-stage stochastic programming where the second stage is demanding computationally.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper deals primarily with optimizing load planning for rail transportation, which directly falls under the Transportation sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: We consider a myopic, two-stage booking control problem pertaining to cargo capacity management...

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Although not central, the methodologies can also support modeling risks by managing uncertainties in logistics due to climate variability.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: These predictions stem from supervised ML. They account for the stochasticity in the second stage problem...
